title: [MIG-010] Remove the embedded workflow only after verified Vibez adoption
objective: End duplicate workflow maintenance in Fantasy Football without losing project data, audit history or the ability to use Vibez.
inScope: Use the reviewed MIG-002/009 ownership/removal manifest to delete only migrated reusable implementation, redundant core schemas/contracts, engine-only tests/scripts and replaced CI/build wiring. Because this baseline is mostly control-plane code, do not assume every path under src/tests/docs is disposable: classify any later consumer/product additions before removal.

Retain consumer task/requirement/project-contract definitions, configuration, pinned dependency, integration smoke tests, project docs and historical evidence/archive pointers. Library-owned semantic contracts must remain available through the supported installed package. Never remove ignored .agent state, exchanges, stopped canary records or Git history by recursive cleanup.

Update AGENTS/README/bootstrap references to explain the consumer workflow, Vibez maintenance location and historical archive. Keep old issues/PRs accessible; do not close unrelated #75/#78 or bootstrap work merely because files moved.

Block merges that reintroduce copied engine source/schemas or deep imports; retain a lightweight installed-consumer CI contract. Verify the final source-delta ledger and ongoing reusable ownership in Vibez.

Record completion evidence against #74 and the roadmap only after the removal PR satisfies required review/CI/controlled completion. A rollback reverts the cleanup commit or restores the pinned consumer version under the supported quiescent procedure, not history rewriting.
**Expected surfaces:** Only inventoried migrated paths, consumer scripts/build/CI, AGENTS/README/archive navigation, lightweight consumer integration test and source-reference guard.
outOfScope: No deletion of project requirements/configuration, runtime/evidence data, Git history or unrelated code; no disabling required validation/review to make cleanup pass.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: MIG-009 parity, observation criteria, independent reviews and rollback evidence are accepted before removal starts.
AC-02: The final removal manifest accounts for every deleted path and retains all project-owned and historical material.
AC-03: No authoritative duplicate workflow implementation remains; consumer imports/commands resolve only through the pinned supported Vibez surface.
AC-04: Fresh clone/install and full supported consumer journey work without the deleted source; required CI remains enabled.
AC-05: Runtime/evidence/history records are unchanged by cleanup, and old archive/source links remain usable.
AC-06: Ownership/docs and a regression guard prevent future embedded forks; #74 has an evidence-backed completion map.
validationPlan:
Review the deletion diff path-by-path against the ownership manifest. Run fresh-install consumer CI/conformance smoke, reference/deep-import scans and history checksum comparison. Demonstrate rollback from the cleanup commit without modifying runtime data.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
